blurb: The run began with Sea's fourth-quarter 2018 report on February 27, 2019, when the stock hit its first new 52-week high; it rose 53.5% in February. Results beat the high end of the company's own guidance. Garena's Free Fire reached 40 million daily active users, and Shopee's quarterly gross merchandise value was $3.4 billion, up 27.3% from the prior quarter. Games and e-commerce were both scaling, and the stock peaked December 8, 2020.

blurb: SolarEdge bottomed December 24, 2018 and made its first new 52-week high June 13, 2019, after two strong reports. Second-quarter revenue then reached $325 million, up 43%, with third-quarter guidance of $395-$410 million. GAAP EPS fell 48% in the first quarter.

blurb: Universal Display made its first new 52-week high on February 25, 2019, four days after fourth-quarter results on February 21. Quarterly revenue fell about 40% to $70.1 million, which the company blamed on a soft premium smartphone market, heavy Q4 2017 pre-purchases and a new accounting standard. It guided 2019 revenue to $325-$350 million, in line with analyst forecasts near $342 million. The record shows an outlook reset rather than accelerating growth. The stock peaked December 15, 2020.

blurb: Chewy listed June 14, 2019 and hit a base low November 18. Its breakout to a new high came March 30, 2020, as COVID-19 lockdowns lifted pet-supply spending; card data showed daily pet-retailer spending up 21% on average through March 24. Late-March results showed fourth-quarter net sales up 34.7% excluding the extra week, active customers up 27.2%, and first-quarter revenue guidance of $1.50-$1.52 billion versus roughly $1.45 billion expected. It gave no full-year outlook.

blurb: Farfetch bottomed April 2, 2020 and made its first new 52-week high July 9, as lockdowns pushed luxury shopping online. First-quarter revenue rose 90% to $331 million, with China growth in the last two months of the quarter outpacing all of 2019, despite a large loss and suspended guidance. In November 2020 it announced a partnership with Alibaba and Richemont including a $600 million investment; shares rose 11.1% that day. The stock peaked February 19, 2021.

blurb: Revolve hit its low March 23, 2020 and did not reach a new 52-week high until December 7. The turn showed in third-quarter results on November 11, 2020: net sales fell 2% to about $151 million, but net income rose 103% to $19.4 million and adjusted EBITDA rose 66%. Active customers rose 5% to 1.504 million. October sales were down by a high single-digit percentage, so the run rested on profit recovery rather than sales growth. The stock peaked November 18, 2021.
